headline: NVIDIA Rockets 31.48% as Huang's Return Lifts the Whole Market
body_html:
NVIDIA jumped 31.48% on Monday, the story that defined the session, after the company said Jensen Huang is returning as chief executive. The reinstatement followed an intervention by President Trump. It was the largest single-company move of the day by a wide margin and set the tone for everything else on the tape.

The rally spread well beyond one stock. The S&P 500 rose 4.71% and the Nasdaq gained 7.00%, with 603 stocks rising against 58 falling out of 663 tracked. Semiconductors led the rotation, averaging a 12.84% gain, ahead of technology at 5.59%, financials at 5.13% and industrials at 4.57%. Defensive corners lagged: consumer staples edged up 0.23% and energy rose 1.57%.

NVIDIA's suppliers and peers followed it higher. Micron rose 19.04% and TSMC gained 14.08%. Pockets of weakness were rare, led by CrowdStrike, down 8.92%. The session still carried a reminder that the backdrop is not all easy money, as a Federal Reserve official signalled higher rates are likely over time. Tuesday, November 24, will show whether the enthusiasm holds.

briefs.headline: TSMC Bounces 14.08% After a Rough Stretch
briefs.body: The foundry giant rebounded sharply after a steep slide in recent sessions tied to worries about NVIDIA and fresh US chip restrictions on China. Reports that it paused advanced chip shipments to China had added to the pressure. Monday's rally recovered part of that ground.

briefs.headline: Micron Climbs 19.04% as Chip Stocks Catch a Bid
briefs.body: The memory maker surged as NVIDIA's leadership news lifted the semiconductor group. Shares had been sold off earlier, leaving them looking inexpensive against earnings. Commentary on the stock has also focused on a pending test of the company's rhetoric on rival memory designs.

briefs.headline: Connectivity Chipmakers Post Some of the Biggest Gains
briefs.body: Astera Labs rose 23.16% and Credo Technology gained 22.63%, while MaxLinear climbed 21.38% and Semtech added 18.83%. The group, which supplies the plumbing for AI data centres, moved alongside NVIDIA and filled most of the day's top-gainer list.

briefs.headline: CrowdStrike Slides 8.92% Against the Tide
briefs.body: The cybersecurity company was the day's sharpest decliner in a market where only 58 of 663 tracked stocks fell. Burlington Stores dropped 4.15%, and energy names such as Baytex Energy, Texas Pacific Land and Chord Energy each fell roughly 3.4% to 3.5%.

briefs.headline: Megacaps Split as Tesla Outruns Apple
briefs.body: Among the largest companies, Tesla rose 11.46% while Broadcom gained 3.00% and Apple added 1.90%. Beyond NVIDIA and its direct suppliers, gains were far more modest, showing how concentrated the day's enthusiasm was in AI-linked names.

briefs.headline: Fed's Williams Points to Higher Rates Over Time
briefs.body: John Williams of the Federal Reserve said higher interest rates are likely over time to address inflation. The remark landed on a day of exuberance in equities and adds a note of caution for investors heading into Tuesday's session.
